PHASE.NAME: UPGRADE_4 Tool Schema Economy
PHASE.GOAL: Implement T1 progressive tool disclosure and T7 terse tool schemas without breaking default MCP tools/list compatibility.

DATA_FLOWS.FLOW: tools/list request arguments select profile all, verification, planning, implementation, debugging, minimal, or custom before schema serialization.
tools/list style full preserves existing schema descriptions; style terse removes descriptions recursively and reports schema economy metadata.
High or critical context pressure later forces terse schema output while explicit full remains backward-compatible below pressure thresholds.

STEPS.step-1: Add profile classification for every existing MCP tool, including generated grace skill tools.
STEPS.step-2: Parse profile and style from tools/list params and return total_available and total_visible.
STEPS.step-3: Add terse schema transform that strips all description fields while preserving types, defaults, enums, required, items, and nested properties.
STEPS.step-4: Add protocol tests for all, verification, minimal, custom, full, terse, and profile+terse combinations.

VERIFICATION.CHECK: tools/list without profile returns all tools.
tools/list profile=verification returns no more than 10 tools.
tools/list style=terse returns schemas without description fields and at least 60 percent smaller than full.

RISKS.RISK: Skill-provided dynamic tools may not have static profile metadata; default them to implementation plus all rather than hiding them.
Over-aggressive terse transform can remove nested schema structure; recursive retention must keep machine-readable shape intact.
